works.name: ABISS: Evaluating Text-to-SQL Systems Through Agent Interaction
works.summary: Combines an eight-category taxonomy, council-filtered question generation and style-conditioned user simulation to separate diagnosis from final SQL/feedback quality. Oracle labels help, but clarification does not ensure correct SQL. Unanswerability is approximated by council failure, human auditing finds residual SQL-label errors, and simulated users remain cooperative. AIR counts termination after relevant feedback, not successful resolution.

works.name: AmbiSQL: Interactive Ambiguity Detection and Resolution for Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Uses a seven-type taxonomy to detect ambiguity, collect multiple-choice or free-text clarification, maintain preferences and recheck rewritten questions before XiYan-SQL generation. The four-page demonstration provides 40 curated BIRD/TAG examples, not a controlled broad accuracy or user study. Repeated detection does not establish completeness, and the user-facing Abstain option skips a clarification rather than certifying request unanswerability.

works.name: An OMOP-Based Open-Source Text-to-SQL Benchmark Dataset
works.summary: Evaluates OMOP SQL or exact abstention on concept-normalized inputs and a synthetic PostgreSQL database. The test mixes paraphrases of training-seen SQL variations with held-out variations, despite a stronger split claim elsewhere in the paper. High execution and reliability scores therefore concern this bounded protocol; raw entity linking, fully unseen-template transfer and clinical deployment safety are untested.

works.name: ARCS: Towards Precise Text-to-SQL via Structured Disambiguation
works.summary: Combines multiple-choice interpretation selection with numeric-threshold adjustment over six existing databases. Generated questions are author-curated and evaluated through a two-stage user simulator, separate disambiguation/SQL metrics and an eight-person interface study. Global conventions, annotation-relative coverage, non-empty intended outputs and permissive extra-column scoring bound the results; manuscript task counts are inconsistent.

works.name: AtomSQL: Interactive Disambiguation of NL-to-SQL via User-Guided Atom-Level Alignment
works.summary: Exposes disagreements between generated SQL candidates as clause-level atoms aligned with question phrases, then updates per-user preferences to rerank later candidates. The paper is an interface demonstration, not a controlled accuracy or user study. Resolution is limited to the supplied candidates, and its agreement-based scores are not established as calibrated confidence.

works.name: Auditing and Repairing LLM-as-Judge Failures in a Production Text-to-SQL Pipeline
works.summary: Audits SQL-faithfulness judges using distinct enriched, random and active-disagreement samples, then compares replacements and selective routing. Unanimity gains apply to retained cases, and the Qwen–Opus accuracy comparison is inconclusive. One-domain gold and deferred data limit transfer/reproduction; unreconciled appendix cost and count arithmetic preclude treating precise savings or population estimates as established.

works.name: Beyond Correctness: Resolving Underspecification in Agentic Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Externalizes planned clarification questions in a mutable pool that must be asked or explicitly dropped before SQL submission. It improves annotated ambiguity coverage with more questions, but does not always improve execution accuracy. BIRD subsets are filtered for solvability after oracle clarification, and groundedness counts questions mapped to annotated ambiguities rather than proving correct answer incorporation.

works.name: BIRD-INTERACT: Re-imagining Text-to-SQL Evaluation for Large Language Models via Lens of Dynamic Interactions
works.summary: Evaluates 600 Full and 300 Lite tasks with ambiguity chains, dependent follow-ups, changing database state and a guarded user simulator. Models choose clarification and environment actions under budgets; success follows executable tests. Simulator-human alignment is measured across seven systems on 100 tasks. Ground-truth-informed replies, cumulative follow-up scoring and artificial costs bound generalization; simulator refusal is distinct from database unanswerability.

works.name: Boundary-Aware NL2SQL: Integrating Reliability through Hybrid Reward and Data Synthesis
works.summary: Trains SQL generation, clarification, missing-constraint follow-up and refusal with mutated enterprise examples, supervised fine-tuning and task-specific reinforcement-learning rewards. Ent-SQL-Bench combines SQL execution agreement with LLM-judged natural-language responses. Evidence comes from a held-out portion of the authors' synthetic enterprise corpus; response-level clarification scores do not establish successful multi-turn resolution or transfer to unseen domains.

works.name: Bounded Semantic Planning and Deterministic Compilation for Reliable Enterprise Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Constrains an LLM to governed semantic choices and compiles paths, roles and grain deterministically. A small ACME comparison favors the complete system, but semantic knowledge, retries and development exposure differ from the DDL baseline. LLM adjudication, post-hoc exclusions, nonblocking undecidable checks and incomplete public evaluation artifacts limit guarantees and reproducibility.

works.name: Building SQL Equivalence Proofs from Query Rewrite Rules
works.summary: Constructs replayable SQL-equivalence derivations by aligning logical plans and composing admitted rewrite rules. Positive results depend on rule soundness and schema constraints; replay checks the recorded derivation using the same implementations. UNKNOWN does not establish inequivalence. Coverage is measured on selected query-pair corpora, often labeled by execution agreement, rather than user-intent correctness.

works.name: Can LLM Agents Be Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Studies requirement discovery and post-training delivery for one enterprise Oracle Text-to-SQL engagement using a fact-grounded simulated customer. It separates elicited facts, final handoff recovery and deployment gates; two of eight selected delivery configurations pass, but production compilation is not semantic accuracy and the discovery judge audit covers only 51 fact instances.

works.name: Certified Against Which Oracle? Execution Labels Set the Reported Risk of Conformal Abstention for Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Crosses candidate-clustering and calibration oracles to audit marginal-risk abstention on Spider-Realistic. Suite-based labels change reported risk, while blinded expert judgments show that neither execution oracle is a semantic gold standard. Risk reduction mainly changes which questions are answered; schema-disjoint tests are empirical, and independent expert coverage is limited to two checkpoints at one seed.

works.name: CLARITY: A Framework and Benchmark for Conversational Language Ambiguity and Unanswerability in Interactive NL2SQL Systems
works.summary: Generates SQL-grounded ambiguous and unanswerable questions with pivot-to-schema annotations, multiple facets and varied synthetic clarification responses. Evaluation separates binary detection, target localization and SQL recovery; the multi-turn task supplies a completed dialogue, so its results diagnose conversation-conditioned prediction rather than an agent’s live questioning policy.

works.name: Concept based Ambiguity Resolution in LLMs
works.summary: Uses sparse-autoencoder concepts and an approximate path-kernel distance between a question and generated interpretations to detect ambiguity in AMBROSIA-derived inputs. Generated interpretations serve as unambiguous controls, and a separate held-out threshold protocol is not clearly specified. The SQL evidence concerns detection; missing-concept prediction is evaluated separately on API retrieval, without SQL-generation or clarification-success results.

works.name: Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL in Large Language Models
works.summary: Compares verbal, consistency-based and token-probability confidence for generated SQL. SQL-Aware Confidence filters and folds syntax-related token alternatives; product aggregation leads on Spider while averaging leads on BIRD in the reported experiments. Execution feedback helps selected methods, but candidate-confidence calibration is not a guarantee of semantic correctness or a diagnosis of ambiguity and unanswerability.

works.name: Conversational Interaction for LLM-Based Clinical Text-to-SQL: A User Study with Healthcare Professionals
works.summary: Fourteen physicians prefer a conversational interface on MIMIC-IV Demo; pooled pilot/main logs show more clarification for freely composed questions. A post-study review judges 134/186 conversational SQL outputs correct (72.0%), despite high usability. This is not a matched accuracy comparison between interfaces; small-cohort, demo-database and designer-adjudication limits remain.

works.name: Developing and Benchmarking Verification Algorithms to Improve Text-to-SQL Generation
works.summary: Compares round-trip language critique and synthetic-database execution for reference-free candidate verification and selective abstention. Conservative combinations trade coverage and latency for fewer accepted errors. Benchmark audits use verifier-selected samples; table/prose and arithmetic inconsistencies in reported error estimates limit precise risk claims. These methods do not prove semantic correctness or distinguish every unanswerable request.

works.name: Disentangling Ambiguity from Instability in Large Language Models: A Clinical Text-to-SQL Case Study
works.summary: Decomposes interpretation/answer graph variation into ambiguity and conditional-instability scores. Controlled-interpretation experiments improve pooled failure prediction, but the generated-interpretation clinical setting shows no significant advantage over result entropy. Regime-based error concentration motivates clarification or review routing; actual intervention effectiveness and clinical safety are not evaluated, and results depend on generated interpretations and LLM judgments.

works.name: DSABench: Benchmarking Source Discovery, Coordination, and Execution for Multi-Database Agents
works.summary: Provides 815 reviewed tasks for exact database-source selection, coordination and local execution, including 105 two-branch ambiguity tasks. One controlled clarification substantially improves branch-source recovery. Joint scores also include topology-label gates and corpus-specific comparators; retained wording/gold mismatches, only 22 sequential tasks and simulated dialogue limit broader capability conclusions.

works.name: EntSQL: A Benchmark for Grounding Text-to-SQL in Long-Context Enterprise Knowledge
works.summary: Evaluates SQL grounding in long-form business documents with 1,066 aligned Chinese-English examples from five domains in one enterprise. English experiments contrast schema-only, full-document and concise-evidence inputs; limited bilingual subsets and one-model error analysis bound transfer claims. Public databases and input JSON are listed, but gold answers are withheld; clarification and abstention policies are not evaluated.

works.name: Evaluating LLMs on Conversational Text-to-SQL under Chain Ambiguity and Intent Drift
works.summary: Pairs two-layer clarification chains and non-monotonic intent revisions over 514 BIRD anchors, yielding 1,542 samples. Metrics separate layer identification, structural drift and execution success. Drift recognition is an AST-change proxy, and the human audit retains residual validity failures. Results concern two-layer, chain-then-drift simulated dialogues; the linked repository remains a release placeholder.

works.name: FALCON: A Model and Dataset Agnostic Framework for Synthetic Data Generation for NL2SQL Pairs
works.summary: Synthesizes SQLite question–SQL pairs using persona/reserved-word seeding, alignment filtering and optional alternative interpretations. Reported gains concentrate on harder queries, while synthetic-only training loses aggregate Spider accuracy; the ambiguity audit has high specificity but 28.6% recall, and cost savings are estimated rather than measured end to end.

works.name: From Textual Columns to Query Plans: A Unified Relational-Semantic Execution Framework for Hybrid Query Processing
works.summary: OmniTQA diversifies schema mappings and vague-predicate interpretations within plans that combine SQL and LLM operators over structured and textual data. It selects one answer and evaluates reference agreement; ACC@6 is an oracle candidate-coverage measure. The work supports ambiguity-aware grounding, without evaluating user clarification, abstention or exhaustive interpretation recovery.

works.name: KODE: Mining Implicit Domain Knowledge from Historical Experience for Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Mines reusable domain rules from gaps between historical questions and SQL graphs, then applies retrieval, consensus and localized critique. Controlled studies show larger in-domain gains and smaller abstract-template transfer; optional memory backfill retains execution-based errors, so historical defaults and critic acceptance do not certify a new user’s intended semantics.

works.name: LASSO: An LLM-Agent Synthesized System for SQL Validation
works.summary: Builds heuristic SQL test-data strategies through agent-assisted coding and human-reviewed regression tests. It refutes query pairs under sanitized, dialect-adjusted execution comparisons; survival is not equivalence proof. Some benchmark failures informed development, timing excludes external test execution, and the BEAVER unseen check measures non-empty generation for ten queries rather than NL-to-SQL accuracy.

works.name: LatentRefusal: Latent-Signal Refusal for Unanswerable Text-to-SQL Queries
works.summary: Uses a supervised TRGE probe over a frozen LLM’s intermediate activations to gate SQL generation. Experiments train separately for each benchmark and require white-box access; the SQL semantic-entropy baseline approximates equivalence syntactically. Reported probe overhead excludes the backbone pass, and refusal F1 does not certify admitted SQL correctness or zero-shot domain transfer.

works.name: Never the Number: Structural Abstention for AI Systems Whose Answers Are Consumed as Fact
works.summary: Proposes a generative shell around an authored, deterministic question-to-query kernel with user confirmation and refusal outside supported shapes. The report offers a qualitative deployment account and synthetic examples, not quantitative validation. Correctness remains conditional on authored mappings and meaningful confirmation; refusing an unsupported shape does not prove the request is intrinsically unanswerable.

works.name: Node-Level Uncertainty Estimation in LLM-Generated SQL
works.summary: Labels generated SQL nodes by heuristic alignment with a reference AST, then predicts node errors from schema-aware features using LightGBM. BIRD and SynSQL transfer experiments improve aggregate ROC-AUC over token probabilities, with weaker out-of-distribution performance. Missing clauses receive no node label; calibration and downstream repair or selective execution are not evaluated.

works.name: ODUTQA-MDC: A Task for Open-Domain Underspecified Tabular QA with Multi-turn Dialogue-based Clarification
works.summary: Introduces a Chinese real-estate benchmark connecting SELECT/FROM/WHERE underspecification, table retrieval and clarification, plus MAIC-TQA. Its simulator provides canonical corrections only after matching gold detection labels, with optional paraphrasing; results show improved recovery of answerable targets under this controlled protocol, not general unrecoverable-answerability or human-dialogue performance.

works.name: Pervasive Annotation Errors Break Text-to-SQL Benchmarks and Leaderboards
works.summary: Uses an agent-assisted, human-adjudicated audit to identify annotation errors and ambiguity in dated BIRD Mini-Dev and public-gold Spider 2.0-Snow subsets. Re-evaluating 16 agent implementations on 100 corrected BIRD examples changes rankings. Corrections include questions, knowledge and some database rows; disclosed backend substitutions and subset coverage limit claims about current full leaderboards.

works.name: PleaSQLarify: Visual Pragmatic Repair for Natural Language Database Querying
works.summary: Clusters a fixed pool of generated SQL by output similarity and ranks interpretable feature decisions for visual clarification. AMBROSIA tests assume gold-consistent feedback; a twelve-person study uses SQL-familiar participants and small databases. Candidate-pool omissions limit recovery, and reported task completion credits partial subtasks rather than measuring exact original-intent success.

works.name: Policy-Conditioned Constrained Decoding for Column-Level Access Control in Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Masks disallowed column uses during SQL decoding and returns REFUSE for blocked or unsupported continuations. This is policy-conditioned refusal, not intrinsic unanswerability. Coverage counts compliant outputs rather than intent-correct answers; semantic execution is tested separately on permitted-reference queries. Guarantees concern a restricted single-query grammar, and token counts do not establish wall-clock efficiency.

works.name: Post-SQLFix: Property-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated SQL with Runtime Verification
works.summary: Uses static SQL diagnostics and explicit edit contracts to guide repairs, accepting only proposals that reduce violations and preserve monitored structure. It reports fewer residual execution errors than feedback-only repair; guarantees are bounded to the rule family, while full-pipeline accuracy gains and optional empty-result alignment must be distinguished from semantic correctness.

works.name: PremiseSQL: Evaluating Premise Critique and Abstention in Text-to-SQL Systems
works.summary: Pairs flawed queries with originals to measure premise critique and over-refusal under different prompts. Explicit flaw assertions improve detection while suppressing valid-query generation. GEN is coverage, with separate execution validation. Failure-mechanism analyses use selected consensus cases and AI-assisted human labels; they are not population-level causal explanations or evaluations of live clarification success.

works.name: Probing Ambiguity: Adversarial Intent Resolution for Robust Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Uses adversarial interpretation proposals, SQL execution and result-based pruning before generating contrastive clarification. Schema-only limits generation context, while verification still queries the full database. Benchmarks measure interpretation coverage, not user clarification quality or completed dialogue success; current-instance agreement can hide semantic differences, and reported serial API latency is substantial.

works.name: QDA-SQL: Questions Enhanced Dialogue Augmentation for Multi-Turn Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Synthesizes multi-turn dialogues with answerable, ambiguous, unanswerable and non-database questions, then filters and formats them for intent routing and SQL generation. Mixed-type training improves recognition, but ambiguity/unanswerability F1 remains low in the displayed CoSQL experiment. AccS scores nonanswerable turns by category correctness, not clarification quality; absent-value cases are also labeled unanswerable.

works.name: RAQS-SQL: Schema and Value Ambiguity Resolution in Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Combines question-to-column alignment with semantic and hierarchical value matching, and introduces AmbiVal from Spider and BIRD. The approach focuses on schema and value ambiguity; those grounding tasks should be distinguished from evaluating a full clarification dialogue.

works.name: Reasoning about Intent for Ambiguous Requests
works.summary: Trains models with DAPO to produce up to five interpretation–answer pairs, rewarding recall on ambiguous examples and precision on clear ones with ambiguity oversampling. Improves AMBROSIA coverage and transfers to AmbiQT. Human evaluation measures explanation–answer alignment, not correctness or user preference; over-generation, finite interpretation limits and simulated clarification comparisons remain important boundaries.

works.name: Reliable End-to-End Text-to-SQL Generation
works.summary: RTS++ clusters candidate SQL by execution results and combines execution entropy with reranker scores for conformal calibration, abstention and user selection. Spider/BIRD results report accuracy on the non-abstained subset and assume accurate feedback. The stated prediction-set coverage should not be read as an unconditional semantic-error guarantee; candidate coverage, calibration validity and database-result normalization constrain interpretation.

works.name: Rethinking Text-to-SQL: Dynamic Multi-turn SQL Interaction for Real-world Database Exploration
works.summary: Evaluates SQL agents in dialogue with a simulated user and a mutable SQLite database, using final-state comparison and all-runs-success Pass^k. Tasks pursue a fixed, fully specified hidden objective through dynamic interaction; the paper reports full expert review but contains an unresolved total-versus-short/long count discrepancy, so neither perfect dataset correctness nor unrestricted intent evolution is established.

works.name: ROSE: An Intent-Centered Evaluation Metric for NL2SQL
works.summary: Judges executable SQL with a Prover-Refuter cascade that treats reference SQL as challenge evidence and uses explicit acceptance rules for ambiguity. ROSE-VEC validates agreement on 585 expert-consensus cases; discarded disagreements, reference-visible human annotation and backbone-dependent diagnostic precision limit generalization. Observed leaderboard changes do not isolate model improvements from system engineering.

works.name: RTS-SQL
works.summary: RTS uses hidden-state conformal checks during schema linking; RTS++ adds execution-result clustering, entropy and reranking for selective full-query generation.

works.name: Same SQL, Different Decision: Aggregate Risk Hides Cross-Lingual Instability in Text-to-SQL Verification
works.summary: Audits English-calibrated execute/defer thresholds while holding SQL, schema and execution labels fixed across seven question languages. Aggregate risk can hide unsafe promotions and lost automation. Score transport restores coverage more easily than individual decisions; English pivot translation helps unevenly. Results are verifier/threshold-dependent and conditional on imperfect translations and instance-based labels, not end-to-end multilingual generation.

works.name: SCARE: A Benchmark for SQL Correction and Question Answerability Classification for Reliable EHR Question Answering
works.summary: Balances 4,200 question/candidate-SQL triples across correct, incorrect, ambiguous and unanswerable cases on three EHR schemas. It measures preservation, correction and input classification jointly; baseline prompts can include execution results and annotation evidence. Results expose model-dependent trade-offs, not execution-free verification, realistic clinical prevalence, completed clarification or deployment safety.

works.name: Schema-Free Text-to-SQL: Learning Enterprise Database Structure from Query Logs
works.summary: Mines query-log relationships and business entities for graph-based context retrieval in an internal enterprise study. Its public BEAVER evaluation instead reconstructs the graph from schema metadata. The reported 95.7% is execution validity, not answer accuracy; small-sample expert preferences and LLM rubric scores do not establish complete ambiguity resolution or abstention.

works.name: SOMA-SQL: Resolving Multi-Source Ambiguity in NL-to-SQL via Synthetic Log and Execution Probing
works.summary: Uses candidate-SQL disagreement, an ambiguity taxonomy and executed probes to repair a selected query; optional synthetic-log clarifications supply extra grounding. Reported execution gains support the probing pipeline, but log experiments derive supervision from benchmark gold SQL without a clear disjointness protocol, and database evidence cannot by itself verify a user’s unstated intent.

works.name: SpotIt+
works.summary: Searches for database counterexamples to candidate/reference SQL equivalence using bounded verification and database constraints.

works.name: SpotIt+: Verification-based Text-to-SQL Evaluation with Database Constraints
works.summary: Combines mined database constraints, LLM filtering/repair and bounded SQL equivalence checking. BIRD experiments recheck execution-accepted query pairs under five-row bounds and set semantics; examples show how constraints change counterexamples. Realism remains best effort, users must validate domain assumptions, and neither bounded agreement nor agreement with a potentially faulty reference proves unrestricted correctness.

works.name: SpotIt: Evaluating Text-to-SQL Evaluation with Formal Verification
works.summary: Extends bounded SQL equivalence checking with string/date support, backend-validated counterexamples and cross-system reuse. Finds differences missed by execution matching on BIRD and SQLite Spider 2.0. Such differences can expose incorrect predictions, flawed gold queries or valid alternative interpretations; bounded passes, unsupported queries and timeouts must remain distinct from proof of user-intent correctness.

works.name: SQLoom: Set-Contrastive Learning of Syntactic, Semantic, and Logical Dependencies for Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Uses parser checks and schema-legal counterexample databases to construct contrastive SQL training supervision, and reports correcting 378 Spider annotations including underspecified questions. Its relevance is verification-grounded supervision and label quality: query disagreement does not establish which interpretation satisfies a user, and reference/LLM checks remain assumptions. No clarification or abstention policy is evaluated; official code/data downloads were not verified.

works.name: SQLStructEval: Structural Evaluation of LLM Text-to-SQL Generation
works.summary: Measures canonical SQL-structure variation across repeated generations and input perturbations. A full JSON-to-SQL pipeline improves execution accuracy and correct-output concentration while increasing overall diversity. Metrics also reflect parse coverage; structural variation is not itself error. Selected error-case analyses are not population rates, and the notes flag an inconsistent COUNT(1) label in the pipeline illustration.

works.name: TACO: A Benchmark for Open-Domain Text-to-SQL with Ambiguous and Cross-Database Queries
works.summary: Combines restricted smart-city examples and synthetic public-data queries to test table discovery and cross-database SQL planning. TACO-SQL rewrites requests without user confirmation; evaluation is single-turn execution agreement. Oracle-table and retrieved-table ablations differ, public release coverage differs from the paper total, and no all-interpretation or clarification-dialogue guarantee is established.

works.name: Text-to-SQL Models Make Choices Without Saying So
works.summary: Builds 204 controlled request triples on 12 existing databases to separate computing an interpretation from disclosing a calculation choice. Models often compute both specific versions but return one for the open request; deciding before separate generation and preserving wording improve coverage. Tests cover one choice/two references, score precision on clear requests, and use simulated users and reconstructed product baselines.

works.name: TraceSQL: Traceable Answerability Estimation for Reference-Free Text-to-SQL Verification
works.summary: Learns candidate-SQL verification from LLM-generated diagnostics and SQL-structure signals, retaining feature-to-evidence links. Held-out BIRD tests improve aggregate F1/AUC over GradeSQL-7B but reject many reference queries. The 67-feature pipeline uses reference-execution training labels and substantial upstream LLM assessment; traceability does not establish semantic correctness or general request answerability.

works.name: Tracing Recurrent and Emergent Hallucination Patterns in Decomposed Text-to-SQL Generation
works.summary: Decomposes BIRD-mini SQL into executable sub-query paths and diagnoses six rule-based error categories across five models, with and without prior history. Separates categories recurring at the final step from those first detected there. Labels are reference-sensitive structural heuristics, not definitive semantic judgments; conditional recurrence is neither causal error propagation nor calibrated uncertainty, and no mitigation is tested.

works.name: Trajectory-Derived Confidence for Reliable, Resource-Aware Clinical Text-to-SQL Agents
works.summary: Learns per-agent confidence from execution trajectories to refuse, stop early or withhold final answers. EHRSQL utility improves at low error penalties, while higher-penalty results approach always refusing. Primary labels use an LLM judge, answerability has strong question-template shortcuts, and reported agent-step savings exclude monitor overhead; the study does not establish clinical deployment safety.

works.name: Verifying Text-to-SQL Queries under Changing Business Semantics
works.summary: Revalidates fixed SQL against a requested business revision and knowledge cutoff using legal counterexample ledgers and exact monetary semantics. On 32 authored revision families, obligation coverage detects 137/144 discrepancies versus 127/144 for generic ordering; current-only and equal-weight scoring match, so revision-priority gains are unestablished. Evidence remains finite-suite, authored-schema and local-model scoped; no public artifact identifier is assigned.

works.name: What Is a Clarification? Estimating Model-Dependent Input Ambiguity
works.summary: Estimates model-accessible answer sets through answer–clarification–answer consistency. Four-model evaluation includes 96 AMBROSIA requests, with best set-F1 in two SQL settings; response-policy experiments are QA-only. Recovery shares a semantic judge with reference construction and can preserve confident errors. A singleton accessible answer does not establish that the user’s request has only one valid interpretation.

works.name: What Predicts Correctness in Text-to-SQL? A Selective-Prediction Study
works.summary: Compares sampled agreement, model scores and verifier signals for selective SQL answering. Frozen judges and calibrated ensembles rank reference-execution correctness well on selected BIRD/Spider slices; trained verifiers transfer less well to held-out schemas. These are empirical, configuration-specific results. The notes flag abstract/table and figure/caption inconsistencies; calibrated abstention does not establish request answerability.

works.name: When the Bottleneck Shifts: Diagnosing and Closing Information Gaps in Interactive Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Routes schema inspection, typed knowledge retrieval and clarification before SQL generation, with retry control and follow-up state carry. Reports 51.0% first-phase and 37.0% two-phase success on BIRD-Interact Lite. Gold-derived coverage is a diagnostic proxy; inconsistent budget totals and value-feedback case descriptions limit exact efficiency and equal-protocol comparisons.

works.name: Calibrating LLMs for Text-to-SQL Parsing by Leveraging Sub-clause Frequencies
works.summary: Combines token probability and syntactic sub-clause agreement across sampled SQL candidates using supervised multivariate Platt scaling. It improves aggregate calibration and error ranking in the tested Spider/BIRD settings, but requires labeled calibration data and additional generations. Scores concern candidate correctness, with an underspecified correctness evaluator; they do not establish request answerability or guaranteed abstention risk.

works.name: CLEAR: A Parser-Independent Disambiguation Framework for NL2SQL
works.summary: Builds candidate schema mappings, collects multiple-choice selections and rewrites both question and schema for a downstream parser. CLAMBSQL adds ambiguity and clarification annotations, so the evaluation depends on those annotated choices rather than unconstrained conversations.

works.name: Confidence Estimation for Error Detection in Text-to-SQL Systems
works.summary: Studies confidence-based rejection and calibration on English PAUQ distribution shifts and EHRSQL unanswerable requests. Selectors fit on a known portion of shifted data. Unsupported questions are often easier to reject than incorrect SQL for relevant requests, while compositional shifts cause substantial rejection of correct answers. Post-hoc calibration improves scores but does not remove this coverage cost.

works.name: Disambiguate First, Parse Later: Generating Interpretations for Ambiguity Resolution in Semantic Parsing
works.summary: Generates default natural-language readings, infills missing interpretations, then parses each into SQL. It improves reference-reading coverage over prompting and transfers across AmbiQT and AMBROSIA, but does not dominate in-domain fine-tuning on full coverage. Incorrect initial readings are retained, and the unambiguous evaluation does not penalize extra queries; coverage is not actual user-intent selection.

works.name: Evaluating and Enhancing LLMs for Multi-turn Text-to-SQL with Multiple Question Types
works.summary: Combines CoSQL-derived and generated conversations with four question types, and tests a selector/detector/decomposer/refiner framework. TDEX scores SQL execution on answerable or ambiguous turns and classification on other turns; response quality uses an LLM judge. Results concern a curated, imbalanced dialogue test, with numerical inconsistencies in some detailed reporting and no unrestricted real-user validation.

works.name: Fundamental Challenges in Evaluating Text2SQL Solutions and Detecting Their Limitations
works.summary: Separates Text-to-SQL solution errors, benchmark-data defects and matching-metric biases, illustrating how ambiguity, missing schema information and false presuppositions distort evaluation. A multi-LLM disagreement heuristic supports manual Spider inspection; the resulting example lists are incomplete and do not constitute a validated automatic detector or production noise estimate.

works.name: Grounding LLMs for Database Exploration: Intent Scoping and Paraphrasing for Robust NL2SQL
works.summary: Combines in-scope/partial/out-of-scope classification with entity-preserving paraphrase augmentation. Component tests use constructed scope cases; search worsens BIRD scope detection, and augmentation helps BIRD/BI but not Spider. The paper leaves integration into a complete system handling complex joins/nesting to future work, so partial-scope detection is not evidence of successful interactive recovery.

works.name: Interactive Text-to-SQL via Expected Information Gain for Disambiguation
works.summary: Selects clarifications by expected entropy reduction over weighted SQL candidates, then filters candidates using feedback. Experiments use gold-based simulation and a confidence-filtered Spider subset. Results depend on candidate coverage and probabilities; one-step EIG does not establish universally optimal dialogue effort. The notes flag conflicting exact-match baselines and incomplete artifact/experiment specification.

works.name: Learning to Clarify: Multi-turn Conversations with Action-Based Contrastive Self-Training
works.summary: ACT trains clarify-versus-answer behavior with action-contrast preferences and simulated multi-turn outcomes, improving small-data adaptation of Zephyr on AmbigSQL and two QA tasks. AmbigSQL pairs Spider requests with synthetic underspecification; its user simulator sees the target SQL, so reported recovery measures simulated clarification rather than human interaction.

works.name: Leveraging LLM-Generated Schema Descriptions for Unanswerable Question Detection in Clinical Data
works.summary: Predicts table relevance using LLM-written schema descriptions, a T5-small encoder and supervised relevance heads, then thresholds the maximum score before SQL generation. EHRSQL-2024 experiments keep the same 17 tables across splits. Description ablations improve detection, but unseen schemas, database-content-dependent answerability and downstream SQL correctness remain unvalidated.

works.name: LinkAlign: Scalable Schema Linking for Real-World Large-Scale Multi-Database Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Separates database retrieval, irrelevant-schema filtering and table/column grounding, with pipeline and multi-agent variants. Its synthetic AmbiDB expands Spider with overlapping schemas while retaining clues for one intended database; this stresses automatic schema selection rather than live clarification, and gains vary across exact-match, location and recall metrics.

works.name: NL2SQL-BUGs: A Benchmark for Detecting Semantic Errors in NL2SQL Translation
works.summary: Benchmarks candidate-SQL correctness and a nine-category/31-subtype error taxonomy using screened BIRD references and expert annotations. Correctness labels primarily use current-database execution agreement, which can miss accidental matches. Its Type-Specific Accuracy is recall-like and does not penalize extra type predictions by itself; query answerability and clarification are separate tasks.

works.name: ParSEval: Plan-aware Test Database Generation for SQL Equivalence Evaluation
works.summary: Generates small test databases from logical-plan coverage constraints using symbolic and hybrid solving. Pair-aware tests use both candidate and reference queries; reusable gold-only suites are a separate protocol. Experiments improve counterexample discovery, but NULL multiplicities, special functions and extra joins can escape testing. Passing finite tests does not prove unrestricted equivalence or validate the reference intent.

works.name: PRACTIQ: A Practical Conversational Text-to-SQL dataset with Ambiguous and Unanswerable Queries
works.summary: Builds synthetic dialogues by mutating Spider schemas/values and reverse-generating user replies from target SQL. Baselines classify question types and generate SQL with supplied clarification, sometimes after the request changes. Missing-value unanswerability is a benchmark convention, not a rule for all empty results; scripted dialogue and inconsistent printed totals limit broader claims.

works.name: Query Carefully: Detecting the Unanswerables in Text-to-SQL Tasks
works.summary: Adds schema-aware refusal rules and retrieved answerable/unanswerable examples to a biomedical SQL pipeline. Evaluation covers 99 OncoMX development questions and 80 synthetic, author-reviewed negatives; negative demonstrations are retrieved from that same pool excluding the current question. Balanced prompts help detection, but execution-error repair can increase wrong results and missing values or column ambiguity remain difficult.

works.name: RAG-based Unanswerable Question Detection in Clinical Text-to-SQL
works.summary: RaQAD retrieves semantically similar examples for few-shot LLM prompts that classify whether clinical database questions are answerable, without additional model training. The institutional abstract reports clinical experiments and adaptation to schema changes. This supports inclusion as an answerability-screening method; detailed evaluation conditions, downstream SQL correctness and clarification behavior were not verified from full text.

works.name: Reliable Text-to-SQL with Adaptive Abstention
works.summary: Detects schema-linking branching tokens with hidden-state classifiers and conformal prediction, then abstains or seeks surrogate/human feedback. Linking and downstream SQL improve in tested settings, but guarantees concern marginal label-set coverage under calibration assumptions. Human help, hidden-state access and task-specific training are required; distribution shift and full-query semantic correctness are not guaranteed.

works.name: SIMBA UQ: Similarity-Based Aggregation for Uncertainty Quantification in Large Language Models
works.summary: Learns confidence from similarities among sampled responses, optionally adding token-probability features. SQL experiments use reference-execution labels and random in-domain train/test splits on Spider, Spider-Realistic and BIRD. Calibration gains are stronger than selection/discrimination gains; matched sampling, labeled examples and untested distribution-shift behavior limit deployment claims.

works.name: Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows
works.summary: Benchmarks enterprise-style SQL workflows involving large schemas, multiple dialects, external definitions and dbt projects, with a tool-using Spider-Agent baseline. Workflow instructions can be underspecified relative to supplied context, but evaluation uses task-specific output checks rather than dedicated clarification or abstention metrics; Lite questions deliberately reduce ambiguity.

works.name: SQLens: An End-to-End Framework for Error Detection and Correction in Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Combines database and LLM signals through weak supervision to diagnose clause-level errors and guide sequential SQL repairs. BIRD/Spider experiments report net fixes alongside regressions, with correction evaluated on syntactically valid candidates. Empty-result and schema heuristics can flag valid SQL; the system remains an asynchronous debugging aid, not an answerability or correctness guarantee.

works.name: SQUAB: Evaluating LLM robustness to Ambiguous and Unanswerable Questions in Semantic Parsing
works.summary: Combines table-pattern detection, SQL transformations and LLM verbalization to generate ambiguity and refusal tests. Its evaluation is single-table; cost savings use estimated annotation costs. Out-of-scope unanswerability is not programmatically proved, and the small expert audit identifies category-specific failures. Generated tests therefore need semantic review before being treated as reliable evaluation labels.

works.name: The Case for Intent-Based Query Rewriting
works.summary: Proposes alternative SQL over available schemas when a query's original tables are inaccessible, allowing different results that raters consider useful for a similar analytical goal. Ten authored SQL queries and three-rater judgments test rewrite plausibility across 957 table schemas. Actual-data answer correctness and query-execution speed are not evaluated; correlated substitutes do not guarantee semantic equivalence or faithful recovery of the original request.

works.name: The Consistency Hypothesis in Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models
works.summary: Formalizes and statistically tests whether agreement among sampled generations predicts correctness, including Spider, Spider-Realistic and BIRD, then evaluates similarity aggregation for confidence and selective generation. Support varies with model, dataset and similarity definition. SQL correctness is labeled by reference-result agreement on the supplied database; consistency is not a semantic proof or a diagnosis of request answerability.

works.name: AMBROSIA: A Benchmark for Parsing Ambiguous Questions into Database Queries
works.summary: Benchmarks scope, attachment and vague interpretations using human questions over constrained synthetic databases. Models receive complete schema/data dumps; best zero-shot interpretation recall is 30.7%, with only 1.9% AllFound. Resolved-input baselines reveal ordinary parsing difficulty. Evaluation flattens outputs to value sets, so matching is relaxed execution evidence; the benchmark does not test unanswerability or live clarification.

works.name: MultiSQL: A Schema-Integrated Context-Dependent Text2SQL Dataset with Diverse SQL Operations
works.summary: Extends CoSQL-derived dialogues with schema/content mutations and longer context, using GPT-4 generation followed by human correction. It introduces heuristic context-aware and database-state matching. History/refinement gains depend on model and operation, and Llama outputs receive GPT-3.5 extraction assistance. The fixed corpus tests state tracking rather than autonomous clarification or unanswerability decisions.

works.name: NL2SQL is a solved problem... Not!
works.summary: Studies ambiguity and semantic mismatch in enterprise NL2SQL, including a two-annotator KaggleDBQA audit and questions paired with an unrelated database. Introduces Archerfish and a relaxed execution metric that permits selected output differences. Agreement is not ambiguity-detection accuracy, the mismatch test does not establish general answerability, and relaxed matching is not semantic equivalence.

works.name: Overview of the EHRSQL 2024 Shared Task on Reliable Text-to-SQL Modeling on Electronic Health Records
works.summary: Compares eight clinical SQL-or-abstain systems on MIMIC-IV Demo, with unseen question templates and added unsupported requests. Reliability Score rewards correct answers/refusals and penalizes wrong attempts; all teams fall below abstain-all under its most severe penalty. Results concern the selected templates and ambiguity-reducing preprocessing, not clinical deployment readiness.

works.name: Sphinteract: Resolving Ambiguities in NL2SQL Through User Interaction
works.summary: Uses Summarize–Review–Ask to identify ambiguities and integrate clarification feedback into SQL. Benchmark gains use a gold-SQL-informed feedback oracle; the 11-person, SQL-familiar user study separates own-intent tasks from a second gold-visible phase. Reported gains are percentage-point changes, and neither simulator scores nor the gold-visible study establish novice deployment reliability.

works.name: TrustSQL: Benchmarking Text-to-SQL Reliability with Penalty-Based Scoring
works.summary: Evaluates correct SQL and abstention jointly with penalty-based scores on feasible/infeasible questions. Results depend on the chosen penalty and balanced test prevalence: abstain-all scores 50%, so coverage must accompany reliability. Ambiguity resolution is outside scope, and preprocessing removes empty-result cases and implicit context. A positive score is not evidence of deployment safety.

works.name: Benchmarking and Improving Text-to-SQL Generation under Ambiguity
works.summary: Constructs two SQL references per question through four controlled Spider-schema perturbations. LogicalBeam varies join/selection plans and restricts template infilling to schema-name diversity, improving top-five coverage. Evaluation measures candidate availability against the constructed alternatives, not clarification-policy quality or selection of a real user's intended reading; gains and ablation effects vary by ambiguity type.

works.name: Calibrated Interpretation: Confidence Estimation in Semantic Parsing
works.summary: Audits raw token and program confidence across semantic parsers, including Spider and CoSQL. SQL models appear more overconfident than dialogue parsers, while a separate Spider test-suite comparison reduces measured SQL overconfidence relative to exact matching. Teacher-forced token diagnostics, generated-sequence confidence and correctness metrics must remain distinct; clarification and safe-abstention policies are not evaluated.

works.name: Data Ambiguity Strikes Back: How Documentation Improves GPT’s Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Studies value consistency, table coverage and row granularity using GPT-4 on 45 questions from two KaggleDBQA databases. Documentation and query clarifications are manually derived with reference-answer access, and benchmark answers are also corrected. Results support the value of explicit data semantics under this curated setup; they do not establish automatic documentation quality, broad transfer or a live clarification policy.

works.name: Know What I don’t Know: Handling Ambiguous and Unanswerable Questions for Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Uses SQL-derived weak supervision to label problematic question spans, ground concepts and generate template explanations. Its six-category taxonomy is broader than NoisySP synthesis, which mainly creates column ambiguity and missing-column cases. Commercial evaluation uses failed requests; ordinary-query SQL tests are separate, and no complete clarification-to-SQL policy is established.

works.name: Non-Programmers Can Label Programs Indirectly via Active Examples: A Case Study with Text-to-SQL
works.summary: APEL asks non-programmers to choose outputs on small, informative synthetic databases, then updates a distribution over candidate SQL programs. An 11-participant study on 240 Spider utterances improves annotation accuracy from 59% to 75% and reveals reference-label errors; candidate coverage and human interpretation remain limits, and downstream training gains were not evaluated.

works.name: EHRSQL: A Practical Text-to-SQL Benchmark for Electronic Health Records
works.summary: Builds temporal and cohort SQL tasks from hospital-staff questions over processed MIMIC-III/eICU data, with held-out unanswerable requests that can include ambiguity. Templates are shared across splits, and the strongest baseline uses the known unanswerable proportion. Time shifts, shuffled patient-associated records, synthetic costs and annotation assumptions limit clinical and cross-hospital interpretation.

works.name: NL-EDIT: Correcting Semantic Parse Errors through Natural Language Interaction
works.summary: Predicts clause-level SQL edits from feedback, explanations and schema context, using synthetic pretraining and SPLASH. One-turn correction improves, but 16.93% of test examples gain errors. Its representation/evaluation ignores condition values and restricts subquery structure; structural progress does not guarantee semantic preservation or faster multi-turn convergence. Cross-parser gains decrease with stronger base parsers.

works.name: Did You Ask a Good Question? A Cross-Domain Question Intention Classification Benchmark for Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Classifies schema-question pairs into answerable, improper, missing-knowledge, ambiguous and Non-SQL categories using transformed corpora and a balanced, manually checked cross-schema test set. Non-SQL partly reflects the grammar supported by contemporary parsers, not absolute SQL impossibility. Evaluation concerns input triage only; SQL correctness and recovery dialogues are not tested.

works.name: Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-SQL with Distilled Test Suites
works.summary: Distills small database test suites that distinguish mutated neighbors of a reference query, improving evaluation beyond single-database agreement and exact-form matching. Tests approximate equivalence, not proof, and can miss prediction-only branches or unstated domain constraints. Historical comparisons substitute gold values; the 100-example human check covers selected metric disagreements, while Appendix A.3 documents a remaining false positive.

works.name: Speak to your Parser: Interactive Text-to-SQL with Natural Language Feedback
works.summary: Pairs Spider parser errors with explanations and short human correction feedback to evaluate one-round parse repair. Correction uses exact set match; end-to-end scores are derived from initial successes and explanation-supported failures. The reported human ceiling estimates feedback completeness, not observed human SQL repair. Fully specified inputs distinguish this task from ambiguity detection and autonomous clarification.

works.name: “What Do You Mean by That?” A Parser-Independent Interactive Approach for Enhancing Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Aligns a question with a template-based restatement of predicted SQL, asks multiple-choice questions and rewrites the input for a black-box parser. Five-parser experiments include a 30-volunteer Spider study with smaller gains than simulation. The simulator uses reference-filtered options and searches answer combinations, so its results are idealized; candidate menus and supported rewriting rules constrain generality.

works.name: CoSQL: A Conversational Text-to-SQL Challenge Towards Cross-Domain Natural Language Interfaces to Databases
works.summary: Collects Wizard-of-Oz database dialogues with SQL, result descriptions, ambiguity and unsupported-request acts. Database-disjoint tasks evaluate SQL state tracking, successful-query response generation and user-act prediction. Tracking receives recorded clarifications after user affirmation; the paper explicitly leaves clarification-quality evaluation outside its tasks. Response BLEU and human logical correctness rank baselines differently.

works.name: Model-based Interactive Semantic Parsing: A Unified Framework and A Text-to-SQL Case Study
works.summary: Wraps a base parser with uncertainty-triggered yes/no questions and feedback-constrained decoding. WikiSQL and Spider simulations improve accuracy, but human results are smaller and metric-dependent: SQLova execution accuracy slightly decreases without additional information. A separate condition exposes gold SQL, so its stronger result should not be treated as ordinary user clarification.

works.name: SParC: Cross-Domain Semantic Parsing in Context
works.summary: Provides SQL-expert-authored, goal-guided question sequences over disjoint train/test databases, with question-level and whole-interaction exact-set-match evaluation. Context-aware baselines improve, but later turns combine stronger contextual dependence with harder SQL. The corpus tests contextual interpretation, not agent-selected clarification, responsive users or abstention.

works.name: DialSQL: Dialogue Based Structured Query Generation
works.summary: Detects possible SQL errors, asks multiple-choice validation questions and revises a black-box parser's query. WikiSQL experiments include reference-aware simulation and a separate 100-question human study; the latter shows a smaller gain than simulation. Single-table queries, predefined error categories and header-only context limit transfer. The author-linked repository is currently a README-only placeholder.

works.name: Constructing an Interactive Natural Language Interface for Relational Databases
works.summary: Uses dependency parsing, schema/data mappings and user-verified query trees to translate complex requests into SQL, recomputing downstream interpretations after revised choices. A 14-participant, single-domain study improves task completion, but users still accept some wrong answers. Heuristic tree search, fixed condition order and timing restricted to successful tasks limit broader reliability and usability claims.

works.name: IntentSQL
works.summary: Experimental SQLite interface combines bounded model decisions, typed query plans, deterministic SQL compilation, and visible alternative readings.

works.name: LiveSQLBench released Base/Large datasets
works.summary: Released SQL tasks combine database environments, hierarchical business knowledge, and executable tests.

records.name: ABISS: Evaluating Text-to-SQL Systems Through Agent Interaction
records.summary: Combines an eight-category taxonomy, council-filtered question generation and style-conditioned user simulation to separate diagnosis from final SQL/feedback quality. Oracle labels help, but clarification does not ensure correct SQL. Unanswerability is approximated by council failure, human auditing finds residual SQL-label errors, and simulated users remain cooperative. AIR counts termination after relevant feedback, not successful resolution.

unanswerability.detail: Dimension/metric rejection cases remove schema definitions or request undefined metrics.

clarification.detail: Models generate clarification or follow-up responses scored against references; subsequent user replies are not part of the reported protocol.

interaction.detail: Held-out response tasks sampled from the mutated corpus; no measured multi-turn user continuation.

comparisons.domain: Automotive enterprise business intelligence with schema and business-rule context
comparisons.evaluation: Execution-result agreement for SQL; GPT-4o semantic-consistency judgments with three-vote majority for natural-language responses.

evidence.locator: Sections 2.1-2.3 describe enterprise synthesis, ambiguity, constraints, rejection and the held-out benchmark; Section 4.1 defines response-level metrics.
Official benchmark directory lists Ent-SQL-Bench.json; full dataset and database execution were not independently validated.

comparisons.label: Spider-CU

ambiguity.detail: No dedicated linguistic-ambiguity or multiple-interpretation annotations; the task varies allowed column uses under a supplied policy.

unanswerability.detail: REFUSE is a policy-compliance label on the reference SQL, not missing-information or intrinsic-unanswerability ground truth. A compliant alternative may exist.

clarification.detail: The system emits SQL or REFUSE without eliciting user clarification.

interaction.detail: One question, schema and policy per record; the study compares decoding and repair/refusal baselines, not a user dialogue.

comparisons.domain: Cross-domain Spider databases with synthetic column-use policies; the verified release has 20 databases and 1,034 questions.
comparisons.evaluation: Leakage, compliant-output Coverage, SQL-gold Recall, REFUSE-gold Recovery, failures and calls/tokens. Recovery does not establish intent equivalence; semantic execution match is separately reported only for SQL-gold.

evidence.locator: Sections 3–5.4 and Appendices B–D: roles, SQL/REFUSE labels, static inputs, corpus construction and policy-relative scope.
Sections 5.4 and 6.3; Appendix G and Table 11: coverage/recovery definitions and SQL-gold-only semantic execution scoring.
README Repository Layout and License: data/dev.json is Spider-CU, raw Spider is fetched separately, derived data is declared CC BY-SA 4.0; BIRD-CU is forthcoming.
Parsed official JSON: 1,034 records, 20 db_id values, 684 SQL and 350 REFUSE gold labels with per-column policies.
